title: Israeli Strike on Gaza’s Nasser Hospital Kills at Least Six, Officials Confirm – NBC News
body:
An Israeli airstrike hit the surgery wing of Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis late Thursday night, killing at least six patients and medical staff and wounding dozens more, the Palestinian Health Ministry said. The attack, which struck a building that houses operating rooms and intensive‑care units, has intensified calls from the international community for an immediate cease‑fire and renewed scrutiny of the conduct of hostilities in the Gaza Strip.

The strike came amid the fifth week of Israel’s ground and air campaign that began after Hamas militants launched a surprise assault on October 7. Israeli officials have repeatedly said that their operations target “terror infrastructure” and that they take extensive measures to avoid civilian casualties. Yet the Ministry of Health in Gaza, which has been documenting casualties since the conflict erupted, identified the target as a civilian medical facility that was clearly marked with the internationally recognized red cross emblem. The hospital’s director, Dr. Hani Al‑Mansour, confirmed that the blast destroyed a surgical theater and caused the death of three patients undergoing operations, two nurses and a cleaning staff member, while several other patients were evacuated in critical condition.

Humanitarian organizations have condemned the incident as a violation of international humanitarian law, which protects medical facilities and personnel from attack unless they are being used for military purposes. The World Health Organization’s regional director for the Eastern Mediterranean, Dr. Ahmed Al‑Mansoori, warned that repeated strikes on health infrastructure could push Gaza’s already‑fragile health system beyond the point of collapse. “Every hospital hit reduces the capacity to treat the wounded, the sick and the chronically ill, and it erodes the very fabric of civilian protection under the Geneva Conventions,” he said.

Israel’s military spokesperson, however, rejected claims that the hospital was a legitimate target, stating that the strike was aimed at a “terrorist command post” allegedly operating within the compound. The spokesperson added that the Israeli Defense Forces (IDF) employ real‑time intelligence and precision munitions to minimize collateral damage, and that any civilian casualties are “tragic but unintended.” This assertion has been met with skepticism by observers who note that the hospital’s location is well known, and that the IDF’s own mapping of the area shows no evidence of militant activity inside the building at the time of the attack.

The incident has further strained diplomatic efforts to broker a humanitarian pause. The United Nations Security Council convened an emergency session on Friday, where several members called for an immediate investigation by an independent body and urged both parties to respect the sanctity of medical facilities. The United States, a staunch ally of Israel, expressed “deep concern” over the loss of life and pledged to review the circumstances of the strike, while also reaffirming Israel’s right to self‑defence.

As the death toll rises and Gaza’s health system teeters on the brink, the international community faces mounting pressure to intervene before the humanitarian crisis becomes irreversible. Whether the latest strike will catalyze renewed diplomatic engagement or deepen the cycle of retaliation remains uncertain, but the loss of life at Nasser Hospital underscores the urgent need for mechanisms that protect civilians and preserve essential services amid the ongoing conflict.
